newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher on export talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher on export talk.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures ended higher on Thursday, lifted by short covering ahead of the three-day Independence Day holiday weekend and by rumblings of export business in the works, pit sources said.

Soyoil led the way up, climbing roughly half the 1.00 cent per lb limit amid rumors China was in the market for 50,000 to 75,000 tonnes of Argentine soyoil. Also there was talk China was aggressively seeking South American and/or U.S. soybeans and soymeal.
Commercials were again heavy buyers of soyoil and were also active in soymeal which fed talk of export business.
Trade sources noted soyoil was priced competitively in world markets. Soyoil futures tumbled to four-year lows on Monday and the declines attracted pricing interest.
Meanwhile, traders said soyoil values in South America had risen in recent weeks. China bought U.S. soyoil late last week and traders said more business was in the works to Pacific Rim countries.
Soymeal ended $3.80 to $2.00 per ton higher with August up $3.80 at $222.60. Soyoil closed 0.61 to 0.40 cent per lb higher with August up 0.40 at 22.16 cents.

USDA export sales data was also deemed supportive. USDA put net exports of old crop soymeal at 37,100 tonnes, above expectations for 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes. New crop sales at 52,600 tonnes was above expectations for 20,000 to 30,000.
Soyoil export sales at 7,100 tonnes were within the range of expectations from none to 25,000 tonnes.

Commercial buying was a feature in both soyoil and soymeal, traders said. In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought at least 800 lots August and 100 December, floor sources said. Cargill also bull spread 500 August/September at 0.17 cent, premium September. FIMAT Futures bought 700 December and LIT sold 300 August, pit sources said.
In soymeal, Cargill bought a total of 800 lots, split between the July, September, December and January. ADM was also a buyer as were Term Commodities and Continental Grain, traders said.
FIMAT bought 500 lots and Merrill Lynch sold 1,000.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 28,000 lots, below the 42,484 lots traded Wednesday. Soyoil volume was pegged at 24,000 lots, against 24,433 on Wednesday.
